In the Microfreak, how can I copy a sequence from sequence A to sequence B?
Short answer: with the sequencer on, hold the A icon and press the B icon. The display confirms the copy. Hold B and press A to copy the other way.
In the Microfreak, how can I copy a sequence from sequence A to sequence B?
Sequencer on first: Shift + Seq turns the icon strip into Tie/Rest, A, B, Record/Stop and Play/Stop, per Microfreak/UG/13 Sequencer/01 Use.
In the Microfreak, how can I copy a sequence from sequence A to sequence B?
Keeping the copy: patterns are saved with their preset, so save the preset to keep B. Until you do, Shift + B reloads B as last saved, per Microfreak/UG/13 Sequencer/01 Use/01 Select & Play.
In the Microfreak, how can I copy a sequence from sequence A to sequence B?
Why copy: the guide suggests keeping the same melody in both patterns while recording different modulation in each, then switching between A and B as you play.
In the Microfreak, how can I copy a sequence from sequence A to sequence B?
Not documented: copying a pattern into a different preset. The guide covers A and B within one preset only.

What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
Answer/Official from Microfreak/UG/16 Paraphonic Chord Mode and Microfreak/UG/16 Paraphonic Chord Mode/01 Unison, the garden's copy of the Arturia MicroFreak user guide
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?

Short answer: the user guide gives two reasons for a blinking Paraphonic button, Paraphonic Chord Mode and Unison mode. It describes no blink tied to the sequencer, so one of those two modes is most likely on and the sequencer is playing through it.
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
Paraphonic Chord Mode: the button blinks while you set the mode up, then stays on and blinks slowly. One key now plays the chord you entered, built with the intervals of the current scale.
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
Unison: entered with Shift + Paraphonic. The button blinks, and every note plays on all four oscillators tuned slightly apart.
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
Telling them apart: play one key. A chord points to Chord Mode; a single thick note points to Unison. The guide gives no blink rate for Unison, so the rate alone does not separate them.
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
Turning it off: press the Paraphonic button once. The guide gives that step for both modes.
What does it mean in the Microfreak when the Paraphonic button is blinking when I have the sequencer enabled?
Not documented: whether either mode is saved with a preset, and why the blink would show up when the sequencer is enabled. If it appears only once the sequencer is on, the guide does not explain it.

The MicroFreak user guide documents the instrument and its controls.
Congratulations on your purchase of the Arturia MicroFreak!
The MicroFreak is a compact, versatile, semi-modular synthesizer with many distinctive features. It lets you experiment with modular sound construction without patch cords.

The standard MicroFreak and MicroFreak Vocoder Edition share the instrument's core features. The Vocoder Edition has a white casing and a gooseneck microphone; see Microfreak/UG/19 Appendix B Vocoder for its specific features.

Its digital oscillator and analog filter combine a broad range of digital sounds with a warm analog character. A cycling envelope adds modulation options associated with high-end modular systems, and the modulation matrix routes sources to many destinations.
The pressure-sensitive touch keyboard, paraphonic playing, arpeggiator, and assignable modulation destinations make the MicroFreak suited to expressive performance.
The MicroFreak is a USB MIDI Class Compliant device and can connect to compatible devices without installing drivers. Connecting an iPad may require a camera connection or USB-to-Lightning cable.
Two paraphonic sequencers can record and play up to four voices at once, sharing one filter; each sequencer has four modulation tracks.
Check the Arturia website for current firmware, MIDI Control Center, tutorials, and FAQs.

Learning the MicroFreak comes through experimenting, asking questions, and trying ideas. Take time to understand its functions one by one; random tweaking without knowing what is changing can make it harder to stay interested.
Test what you learn as you go. Understanding the instrument helps you create the sounds you imagine.
